name: RoboWorld
summary: RoboWorld uses a video world model as the evaluation environment itself, addressing the two things that normally disqualify that idea: world-model error makes the verdict unreliable, and generation is too slow to run many rollouts. It pairs a fast autoregressive video world model with vision-language scoring that judges task progress from generated rollouts, and introduces step forcing, which combines anchored and one-step self-forwarded contexts to cut train-test mismatch while preserving action-observation dynamics. Agreement with real-robot evaluation reaches Pearson r = 0.989 and Spearman rho = 0.970 across tasks and environments.
innovation: Step forcing, which keeps long generated rollouts on distribution without destroying the action-conditioning that makes them evaluations rather than videos.
Vision-language progress scoring, so the judge does not need a hand-written success detector per task.
matters: The strongest correlation with real-robot results yet claimed for a purely generative evaluator, and it needs no simulator assets at all — the counterpoint to MolmoSpaces' 230k hand-built environments.
limits: A learned evaluator can be gamed by a policy optimized against it, in the way learned reward models are.
Correlation is over the policy set tested; unusual policies may fall outside the world model's competence.
lineage: Video world models in the DreamZero and Cosmos line, repurposed from control to evaluation.
